# A column-selecting grid's column highlight does not follow a cell edit

## Context

Leaf of #18762, the column twin of #18941. Measured in real Chromium (Playwright e2e rig, dev@ab2e7cd17c) on `examples/grid/cellEditing` under its "Cell & Column" and "Cell & Column & Row" models, which no arm has ever switched to. Editing itself works under both (Enter, F2, double-click, Tab, Escape; no page error) — the selection around it does not.

## The Problem

Under "Cell & Column" (identical under "Cell & Column & Row", whose row half #18941 repairs):

| Step | Selected cell | Selected column |
|---|---|---|
| click `firstname` of record 1 | `firstname` / r1 | `firstname` |
| Enter, type, **Tab** | `randomNumber` / r1 (editor there) | **`firstname`** |
| Escape, ArrowRight | `randomDate` / r1 | **`randomNumber`** |
| ArrowDown, F2, Enter | `randomDate` / r2 | **`randomNumber`** |
| double-click `firstname` of record 2, Enter | `firstname` / r2 | **none** |

One Tab inside an edit leaves the highlighted column one column behind the selected cell, and it stays there: every later arrow key moves both by one. A double-click edit ends with a selected cell and no selected column.

## The Architectural Reality

- A click keeps the two together: `src/selection/grid/CellModel.mjs#onCellClick` (`:83`) calls `setSelectedColumns([dataField])` beside the cell toggle.
- The plugin moves the cell alone: `src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs#onTabKey` and `#onEnterKey` call `selectionModel.select(view.getLogicalCellId(record, dataField))`, the base cell select.
- The drift then persists because `CellModel#onNavKeyColumn` (`:126`) steps the column **relatively** — `BaseModel#stepSelectedColumn(step)` starts from the column selected now, not from the selected cell's.
- `BaseModel#setSelectedColumns(dataFields)` is the absolute setter; it returns false and repaints nothing when the selection is unchanged.

## The Fix

In `CellEditing#startEdit`, beside the row rule #18941 adds: a model that selects columns follows the edit by its column — `selectionModel.selectsColumns && selectionModel.setSelectedColumns([dataField])`. Every start passes there (Enter, F2, double-click, Tab's target), so the column is right for as long as the edit lasts and wherever it ends.

Arms on the public example under both models, red on dev: after Tab the selected column is the editor's; ArrowRight after the edit keeps cell and column together; a double-click edit ended by Enter leaves its column selected.

Stacks on PR #18943 (same block of `startEdit`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Under "Cell & Column" and "Cell & Column & Row", the selected column is the edited cell's column after Tab, and after an edit started by double-click.
- [ ] An arrow key after the edit moves the selected cell and the selected column together.
- [ ] Models that select no columns are untouched: the grid e2e and component tiers stay green.
- [ ] The arms are red on dev and mutation-pinned.

## Out of Scope

- Making `CellModel#onNavKeyColumn` derive the column from the selected cell instead of stepping it. It would self-heal a drift at the next arrow key, but not during the edit that causes it; a separate hardening if wanted.
- The suspended-arrow terminal (@neo-gpt's defect-note of 2026-09-19 12:28Z).

## Avoided Traps

- Selecting the column in `onTabKey` and `onEnterKey` beside each cell select: two call sites, and the double-click start would still be missed.
